beats.headline: Seven slips of paper
beats.text: The AI's special box opens, and it is just seven slips of paper. Carl laughs out loud. A coupon for a free Personal Space, upgraded to level three. Two for a free tier-one environmental upgrade. Two for a free tier-one crafting table. Two for a table upgrade. Katia has received the same, and Mordecai, shown them, has to sit down. Cash them in now, he says: the space and the environmental upgrades travel with you, and so do the tables, which upgrade on their own every time you go down a floor. Save the two table upgrade coupons.

beats.headline: Three spaces make a five
beats.text: Donut drops her coupon on Wendita's counter, and the Bopca's hands tremble: a level-three space. Carl and Katia turn theirs in too, and conjoined, the three give the benefits of a level-five space. The fine print says each coupon is worth at most 250,000 gold and two may not be combined for a single item. One of Donut's buys the Ultra-Stabilized bed, two hours of sleep for full rest. Mordecai makes Carl save his last for the store. They pay 15,000 gold on top, and Wendita accepts the coupons with tears streaming down her face.

beats.headline: Two on the alchemy table
beats.text: Mordecai is hunched over the alchemy table and snaps at them to get back before they contaminate it. He used her two table upgrade coupons on the alchemy table, Donut says; he asked her permission earlier. So the table is now level three. She makes a face.

beats.headline: A level-three makeup table
beats.text: Katia has bought a new table Mordecai told her about, a Makeup Table. At level three she can superimpose the face of any monster, crawler or NPC she has met on the glass, which makes sculpting easier, and it doesn't hurt when she sits at it. Level three? You used your upgrade coupons, Carl asks, trying not to sound horrified. Yes, she did. Mordecai is going to be pissed: he wanted to talk her into using them on his alchemy table. But they were her coupons.

beats.headline: Armorer's table, sapper's three
beats.text: Carl asks the Bopca Nodd for the crafting table menu: a long list, most of it useless, most about 25,000 gold, from the generic Tinker's Table to a Beekeeper Beesuit Mending Station. He slides one of his two free table coupons forward for the one he wants, an armorer's table. Then he presents his two upgrade coupons, hesitates over whether it is the right move, and asks to upgrade his Sapper's table to level three.

beats.headline: Already spent
beats.text: Now that they know how to get to the front, Mordecai says, they only need to wait out the timer and hop down the stairs. Oh, and then give him their table upgrade coupons, so he can boost his alchemy table before they go down a floor. Carl exchanges a look with Katia. They have both already spent the upgrade coupons. Okay, says Carl: they will give him a quick recap, but he has to promise not to smack them again.

beats.headline: A fourth in a different colour
beats.text: The Legendary Hell Comes to Crawler Town box holds, as promised, a set of unenchanted bagpipes, and three third-tier personal space upgrade coupons plus a fourth one in a different colour. That's a town upgrade, says Mordecai: Carl will need it for his castle, and he and Donut already have a lower-tier one each from the Tina quest a few floors back. When Carl pulls the town upgrade coupon out, it tells him little, only that he must go to an owned town to use it.

beats.headline: Three for Shanty Town
beats.text: Shanty Town is controlled by the Princess Posse now, and Baroness Victory calls it a smart trade: it circles Larracos and gives the NPCs an extra layer of security, one the Posse controls. We have three town upgrade coupons, Carl says, one each from the Tina quest and a tier-three one he just got in a box. Can they use them here? Absolutely, says Victory, and they might get something like the Larracos city defense system. But the coupons could also go on their base, and that may be the better choice.
